title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page sits under the heading 'Astuce de Tate sur les cycles décomposables' (Tate's trick on decomposable cycles). Grothendieck abstracts the argument by which Tate showed that, for certain abelian varieties, every Tate class is a product of divisor classes. If the divisor case of the Tate conjecture is known, the full Tate conjecture then follows.

Setup. A is an abelian variety over a field k. It is probably finitely generated or finite (the reference to Frobenius elements suggests so), although the reading 'alg. clos' is uncertain. V = T_ℓ(A)⊗Q_ℓ is a module over the ℓ-adic Lie algebra g of the image of Galois, which Grothendieck calls the 'pseudo-algèbre de Lie'. The marginal 'g(k)=g' records that it depends on k. Let K be an algebraic closure of Q_ℓ and set T_K(A) = T_ℓ(A)⊗K, a module over g_K = g⊗K.

Hypotheses.
(a) Tate's conjecture for divisors holds: H^2(A,Q_ℓ(1))^alg = H^2(A,Q_ℓ(1))^g.
(b) g_K acting on T_K(A) has one of two forms.
- It is 'pseudo-algebraic': the Frobenius eigenvalues are of the form ε q^{1/2} with ε a root of unity. This is the supersingular situation; after twisting, g acts trivially on all of H^*.
- Or T_K(A) = V_1 ⊕ V_2 with each V_i an eigenspace for almost all Frobenius, with different eigenvalues on the two pieces. In other words, g_K acts on V_i through characters λ_1 ≠ λ_2 with λ_1+λ_2 equal to the weight character.

Grothendieck states that both conditions hold for powers E^n of an elliptic curve defined over F_q:
- (a) was checked by Mumford for E×E (the attribution continues on the next page), and (a) for E^n reduces to E×E since NS(E^n) is built from the factors and pairs.
- (b) is immediate for E itself, and (b) is stable under products.

Conclusion (next page). D^{2i} = H^{2i}(A,Q_ℓ(i))^alg = H^{2i}(A,Q_ℓ(i))^G, where D^{2i} is the span of products of divisor classes. The inclusions ⊂ ⊂ are a priori, so it suffices to show the two ends coincide.

Why it works. H^{2i} = Λ^{2i}V^∨ = ⊕_{a+b=2i} Λ^aV_1^∨⊗Λ^bV_2^∨. The weight of the (a,b) summand is aλ_1+bλ_2, and invariance after the Tate twist requires (a−i)(λ_1−λ_2)=0, hence a=b=i. Now Λ^iV_1^∨⊗Λ^iV_2^∨ is spanned by products of elements of V_1^∨⊗V_2^∨ ⊂ H^2(1)^g, which are algebraic by (a). In the supersingular case everything is invariant, Λ^{2i} is generated by Λ^2, and (a) again concludes.

The marginal note 'Par Tate, la première condition est un cas particulier de la seconde' seems to remark a logical relation between conditions (a) and (b) attributed to Tate. Its exact meaning is unclear.
errors: As phrased with Frobenius eigenvalues, 'valeurs propres différentes pour presque tous les Frobenius' is too weak. What is needed is that χ1/χ2 is not a root of unity, i.e. χ1^a χ2^b ≠ q^i for (a,b)≠(i,i). The formulation via characters of the Lie algebra g_K (λ1≠λ2) is the correct one and is presumably what is meant.

The notes do not say how (a) for E^n reduces to the E×E case verified by Mumford. This is standard (NS of E^n is generated by pullbacks from factors and pairs, and Hom(E,E)⊗Q_ℓ ≅ Hom_G(V,V)), but it is left implicit.

There is a split between the two cases. In the supersingular (pseudo-algebraic) case the Lie algebra acts trivially and the eigenspace argument is vacuous; the conclusion instead uses that Λ^• is generated by Λ^2.

ideas.what: If the ℓ-adic Galois Lie algebra acts on V_ℓ(A) through two distinct characters (or trivially), then all Tate classes on A are products of divisor classes, so Tate for divisors implies Tate in all codimensions.
ideas.modern_name: Tate's argument for E^n / abelian varieties whose Tate classes are Lefschetz (generated by divisors); exceptional-class-free criteria
ideas.usually_credited_to: Tate (1965, 'Algebraic cycles and poles of zeta functions'); later criteria by Murty, Ribet, Hazama, Milne; products of elliptic curves over finite fields by Spiess (1999)
ideas.where_published: Not in Grothendieck's published texts as far as I know; the cohomological conjectures are discussed in 'Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles' (1969) without this argument.

ideas.what: Using the Lie algebra of the ℓ-adic Galois image ('pseudo-algèbre de Lie') as the relevant symmetry, with Tate classes defined as g-invariants.
ideas.modern_name: ℓ-adic Lie algebra of the Galois image / Lie algebra of the ℓ-adic monodromy (Tate) group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre (ℓ-adic Lie algebras, 1960s), Bogomolov, Deligne, Serre

ideas.what: Mumford's verification of divisor-Tate for a product of two elliptic curves over a finite field, together with stability of condition (b) under products, yields Tate for E^n.
ideas.modern_name: Tate conjecture for powers of elliptic curves over finite fields
ideas.usually_credited_to: Tate (1965–66), with the divisor case for E×E via Deuring theory; Spiess 1999 for general products

missed.claim: A historical detail: Grothendieck attributes the divisor case for a product of two elliptic curves over F_q to Mumford, and phrases Tate's trick in terms of the Lie algebra of the Galois image with a 'pseudo-algebraic' dichotomy. This is a small record of how the argument circulated around 1965. The mathematics itself is known (Tate 1965; Spiess 1999).
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical attribution only; no new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean abstraction of Tate's known argument (Tate classes generated by divisors when Galois acts through two characters) applied to powers of elliptic curves over finite fields. It is standard and already credited to Tate. The only mildly interesting points are the Lie-algebraic phrasing and the attribution to Mumford.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: likely 'Soit A une VA sur k corps [de type fini?]'. The reading 'corps alg. clos' is doubtful because Frobenius elements are used.
'T_K(A) = T_ℓ(A)' should be 'T_K(A) = T_ℓ(A)⊗K' (scalar extension), consistent with the following line g_K = g⊗_{Q_ℓ}K.

The bracket after b) likely reads '[i.e. les valeurs propres des Frobenius sont de la forme ... ε racine de l'unité]', and the eigenvalue expression is ε q^{1/2} (or with exponent −1/2, depending on normalisation).
Margin: 'Par Tate, la première condition est un cas particulier de la seconde' ('condition' rather than 'conj.').
'{+Cu]+}' is probably 'C^n]' or a bracket closing an aside.
'cas a, c, au b) est stable par produits' (next page) is probably 'car a), b) ... et b) est stable par produits cartésiens'.
